newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar floor at 125 yen deemed critical.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar floor at 125 yen deemed critical.

text.p: Technicians who sketched key dollar support at 125 yen predicted that more buyers would emerge if the greenback remains above that level, but a break below could trigger a significant correction.
Ken Boyer, a senior currency strategist at MMS International, noted that 125 yen was a low from mid April and was close to the highs reached by the dollar in February.

Boyer said the dollar is clearly in an "uptrending pattern" as long as 125 yen remains intact. "With the market generally being able to hold above 125, we're going to start to see buying interest emerge again," he added.
The U.S. currency had slid against the yen in overnight dealings amid a strong rally in Tokyo stocks and declines in Japanese yen bond prices.
In New York trading, the dollar deepened it losses but managed to remain above 125 yen. It stood at 125.31/36 yen at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, down from 125.62/72 at the open.
A break below 125 yen support would suggest that a "fairly deep" correction lies ahead, said Martin Autotte, a foreign exchange technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy in Montreal.
The dollar could test an initial target of 124 yen and move towards the 123 yen area, according to Autotte.
The dollar was also under pressure versus the mark on Tuesday following remarks by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke.
On Tuesday, Welteke said the central bank can not welcome a further rise in the dollar.
Meanwhile, a news agency also quoted Welteke as saying he believed the dollar should trade near 1.70 marks and not move above the 1.72 to 1.7350 marks area.
But a spokesman for the state central bank in Hesse, where Welteke is president, stressed that Welteke had not mentioned any specific targets as reported by the other news agency.
The dollar fetched 1.7220/25 marks at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, down from 1.7300/05 at the open.
Autotte noted that a short-term moving average that has been very effective at defining the uptrend in dollar/mark comes in at 1.7220.
Furthermore, he said a daily close below 1.7220 would signal weakness in dollar/mark.
"If we're not able to hold above it, I would be very cautious about dollar/mark...," Autotte said.
